en: The Noble Sūtra on Recollecting the Triple Gem (kha): Sanskrit Text—
The Noble Sūtra on Recollecting the Triple Gem in the Indian Language.
In the Tibetan language: *Phags-pa dkon-mchog gsum rjes-su dran-pa’i mdo* (The Noble Sūtra on Recollecting the Three Jewels).
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ* (Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas).
(*Buddhānusmṛtiḥ*) [Recollection of the Buddha]

Thus is the Blessed One— the Buddha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed Charioteer of men to be tamed, the Teacher of gods and humans— the Buddha, the Blessed One.
That Tathāgata is the natural outflow of merits.
It is the non-perishing of the roots of virtue,
adorned with patience,
and the repository of stores of merit.
Adorned with the secondary marks and blossomed with the primary characteristics,
he is beautiful in his sphere of activity and pleasing to behold.
Delight is the pure faith of those with resolute conviction;
it is unsurpassed by means of wisdom.
Unconquerable by powers,
the teacher of all sentient beings,
the father of the bodhisattvas.
The king of noble persons,
the caravan leader for those setting out for the city of Nirvana,
immeasurable in wisdom.
Inconceivable in its eloquence, pure in its tone,
and delightful in its resonance.
Incomparable in form,
peerless in body,
and unstained by sensual desires.
Unstained by forms, unmixed with the formless,
liberated from the aggregates,
and dissociated from the elements.
Guarded against the sense bases,
severed from the knots,
and liberated from the fevers.
He is completely liberated from craving,
has crossed over the flood, is perfected in knowledge,
and is established in the wisdom of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present.
Not abiding in nirvana,
he stands at the limit of reality;
he stands on the ground that is to be beheld by all sentient beings.
All these are, in particular, the perfect qualities of the Tathāgatas.
(Mindfulness of the Dharma:
The True Dharma is virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end.
virtuous in the middle, virtuous in the end,
with good meaning and well-phrased in expression;
sole,
complete,
and utterly pure.
The Dharma of the Blessed One is perfectly pure, well-expounded, and visible in this very life.
free from fever,
timeless,
leading to the goal,
The Dharma and Vinaya of the Blessed One are to be seen here and now, to be personally realized by the wise, well-expounded, thoroughly proclaimed, and leading to liberation.
Leading to perfect enlightenment,
indestructible, a true stupa,
and a source of refuge.
One who has severed the ties.
(Recollection of the Saṅgha: The noble Saṅgha of the Blessed One is well-practiced.
One who has entered upon the right method,
one who has entered upon the straight path,
and one who has entered upon the proper conduct.
He is one to whom one should join the palms in reverence, one to whom one should show proper respect,
and a field of merit and glory.
The purifier of the great sacrificial fee, the one worthy of being offered into, the one to be offered into.
The Noble Sūtra on the Recollection of the Three Jewels is complete.
